stateless.why: With state kept in shared stores (database, cache), servers are interchangeable. Session state in server memory ties users to one machine.

sticky-sessions.why: Pinning users to servers makes them unequal and fragile. Moving session state to a shared store avoids it.

replica-lag.why: Async replicas trail the primary. Read-your-writes can be ensured by reading recent writers from the primary or waiting for the replica.

index-cost.why: Every write must also update the index, and the index takes space. Index what you query.

hot-partition.why: A partition key with skewed traffic defeats the point of sharding. Pick keys that spread load (e.g. a hash of the order id).

transactions.why: Relational databases give ACID transactions across rows. Many NoSQL stores trade that for scale; payments usually want it.

vertical-limit.why: Bigger boxes are easy until they aren't; horizontal scaling adds capacity and redundancy at the cost of distribution.
